tl;dr it's a culture war in a hobby between people who love the hobby and people who hate that their jobs is writing about the hobby

PC Gaming is a hobby. Like many hobbies, there were traditionally magazines dedicated to hobbyists. People who were active in the hobby tended to have a lot of technical skill and to love the hobby themselves. The internet changed a couple of things

  1. Websites could publish faster and cheaper than magazines
  2. People on blogs could write even cheaper than that

So most of the old magazines (like Computer Gaming World) went under, and even the new online websites like Kotaku had to compete against people giving away content on their own blogs, or twitch, or wherever.

The only way they could compete is to pay their writers even less, because people with the skill to be PC gaming writers also had the skill to get other jobs. So instead they started hiring English majors who didn't care about the hobby, but would write really cheap.

There was a culture clash. The writers actually hated the hobbyists they served. So about a year ago there were a flurry of "gamers are dead" articles, which was these underpaid writers complaining to each other they wished they had better jobs.

Hobbyists ("gamers") were pretty upset, and started boycotting sites which ran those articles.

English majors are heavily exposed to feminist and critical theory, where complaining about misogyny appears impressive. So faced with a problem in the real world, they did what they learned to do in college: accuse critics of misogyny.

The whole mess spun out from there.

I have a ultrabook with the Intel HD 4400. As you know, this is not much of a gaming card, but it can do a decent amount. The issue comes in with variable framerates. Whenever the framerate rises or lowers, it causes timing issues, as the next frame is being rendered sooner/later than expected. If you cap the framerate to the lowest point rounded by ten, and try to make it divisible of your refresh rate*, you will not only get a perceptually smoother game, but your laptop battery will last longer and you will be able to raise the graphics a bit higher than you would've otherwise.

*Try setting monitor to 50 hz if you want 25 fps, however 60hz or 120hz would be good for 40 fps unless you have that setting, be aware though that some monitors fake a refresh rate with dupe frames anyway so you'd be getting a worse result in some cases.

EDIT: using rivatuner included with MSI afterburner gives you the choice of limiting fps. Limiting the fps to your refresh rate can reduce vsync lag considerably for some games, especially OSU.
[LPT] If your computer cannot handle the game consistently at the monitor refresh rate, limit your FPS/framerate
